title: Russell Westbrook appears to announce retirement in social media video
content:
Veteran free agent guard Russell Westbrook has announced his retirement, calling it quits after an 18-year NBA career.

Westbrook, 37, posted a video to social media narrated by actor Michael B. Jordan on Wednesday that featured career highlights.

“Sometimes you don’t even know when you’ve already watched the end,” Westbrook wrote in the accompanying post. “You had to be there. And now it’s over.”

Westbrook doesn’t say a word during the 3 1/2-minute video.

In November, Westbrook became the eighth player in NBA history to record 10,000 assists. He sits fifth on the all-time list with 10,351. In fourth place is LeBron James, with 12,016. Westbrook is also the league’s all-time leader in triple-doubles with 209 and has averaged a triple-double in four different seasons. Drafted with the No. 4 pick in 2008, Westbrook spent 11 seasons with the Oklahoma City Thunder, earning two first-team All-NBA honors and winning the league’s MVP award in 2016-17.

One of the most explosive guards of his era, Westbrook led the league in points per game twice and in assists per game three times.

He spent the 2025-26 season with the Sacramento Kings. He played in 64 games, starting 58, and averaged 15.2 points and 6.7 assists. The Kings, however, went 22-60 and tied the Utah Jazz for the worst record in the Western Conference. That mark earned Sacramento the seventh pick in June’s draft, which it used to select Arkansas guard Darius Acuff Jr.

This story will be updated.
